scope: One Mac-to-VelaNext owned SSH-client interruption and fresh-connection reconciliation of the same deterministic Dagu job
protocol: Freeze local protocol/controller/source/oracle hashes and native binary before execution; refuse prefix reuse.
Launch native dagu start under an owned remote supervisor; Dagu has a separate process session and private file-backed logs, no server or scheduler. Keep its launching SSH client connected.
Wait for native running history and the finalizer-ready marker; verify the exact checkpoint, fsync its closed files and directory, record owned process identities.
Terminate only the recorded local SSH client process. Do not modify routes, firewall, host, distro, shared mux or other client.
Open a fresh independent SSH session; require the same native run ID and unchanged checkpoint with execution_count1.

If still running, release only the finalizer input and await native success. If native aborted/failed, preserve that state, release only finalizer input, and use the supported retry --step finalize with the same run ID once.
Require native succeeded, unchanged checkpoint, exclusive execution claim1, exact completed result, all12 final oracle tests and no owned live processes/listeners.
acceptance: original12-test oracle passes at checkpoint and finalization
same native run ID before disconnect, after reconnect and success
checkpoint/effect count remains1 with byte-identical checkpoint
only own local SSH client interrupted; fresh nonmultiplexed SSH used afterward
owned remote job/controller/processes and listeners cleaned up
limits: Controlled local SSH-client termination is not evidence of a real network outage, power loss, host restart or credential recovery.
Separate remote process session and file-backed logs deliberately remove SSH-pipe dependence; this does not qualify arbitrary foreground processes.
Exclusive checkpoint claim is a local synthetic effect, not distributed exactly-once external side effects.
No model, provider, broker, GPU, global service, authentication or package changes.
Enclosing agent usage remains unknown; no token-savings claim.
